newsitem.title: USA: Former H-P employee files whistle-blower suit.
newsitem.headline: Former H-P employee files whistle-blower suit.

text.p: A former Hewlett-Packard Co. employeee has sued the computer company, contending he was demoted and then fired after discovering environmental and safety violations.
Norman Pawlowski, who said he was hired as the company's "worldwide compliance officer," is seeking $107.5 million in damages in U.S. District Court in Portland.

In the lawsuit filed July 24, Pawlowski said he became aware of so-called violations of the U.S. Toxic Substance Control Act and informed his superiors, but was told to proceed with his work as if no violations had taken place.

Hewlett-Packard officials confirmed that Pawlowski had worked for the company as a chemist at its Corvallis, Ore., site from 1985 to 1996. But at spokeswoman at the company's Palo Alto, Calif., headquarters said executives have not seen the lawsuit and have no comment.
In his lawsuit, Pawlowski said the company wrongly alleged he had committed a crime and attempted to hide it by filing a false document with the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency.

He said he told Hewlett-Packard about other violations of safety and environmental laws, both before and after he was regulatory compliance officer, and was warned against telling his concerns to outsiders.
He said his performance ratings were lowered afterward, and those ratings were used as a basis for his termination.
Pawlowski also named Stanley Landfair, an environmental lawyer, and McKenna & Cuneo LLP, the firm in which Landfair is a partner, as defendants.
